subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Three Gorges Dam: World's Largest Power Station
description: Learn Three Gorges Dam: World's Largest Power Station in one minute.

hook.text: The Three Gorges Dam in China is the world's largest power station. Its 32 turbines generate 22,500 megawatts.

buildup.text: The dam is 7,661 feet long and 607 feet tall. It created a reservoir 410 miles long, submerging 13 cities and 1,600 villages.

discovery.text: The reservoir displaced 1.3 million people. Ancient temples, farmland, and cultural sites were lost beneath the rising water.

twist.text: The weight of the reservoir water is so massive that it actually slowed Earth's rotation by 0.06 microseconds per day.

climax.text: The dam prevents 100 million tons of CO2 annually compared to coal. But its ecological damage to the Yangtze remains debated.

punchline.text: So much water it slowed the Earth. So much power it replaced coal plants.

quiz.question: What unexpected physical effect did the Three Gorges Dam reservoir cause?
options: The water's weight caused measurable earthquakes in the surrounding region
The massive water weight slightly slowed Earth's rotation by 0.06 microseconds per day
The reservoir reflected so much sunlight that local temperatures dropped
